title: Meet Arcy Drive: The Band That Makes ‘Attic Rock’
summary:
Have you ever heard of "attic rock"? It's a new style of music made by a band called Arcy Drive. The name comes from the attic — a place that's messy, full of old stuff, but still special. That's how they describe their sound: a mix of emotional emo and classic garage rock.

Arcy Drive is four friends from Long Island, New York: Nick Mateyunas (singer), Brooke Tuozzo (drums), Austin Jones (guitar), and Patrick Helrigel (bass). They met in school and started playing together just before the pandemic. At first, only Brooke knew how to play drums. The others had to learn fast! But Nick always loved writing songs, inspired by Neil Young and Nirvana.

Their big break came when they turned an old school bus into a tour bus and posted videos online. Soon, they were playing at huge festivals like Lollapalooza and Bonnaroo. Their hit song "Louie" is about Nick's grandfather, who calls everyone "Louie" because he forgets names. How funny is that?

Now Arcy Drive is touring the world. Their music is raw and real — just like an attic.
why_it_matters: It shows that with creativity and friendship, you can turn a simple idea like playing in an attic into a worldwide adventure.
